## Conclusion

Our project aimed to use past Premier League results to predict the final league table of the 2026/27 season.
We trained our models on the 2014/15 to 2024/25 seasons and tested them on the 2025/26 season. Each one of our models predicted match results, which we used to calculate points and create a predicted table. We wanted to find a model that could give a useful prediction, placing greater weight to the top five and the teams at risk of relegation.

To compare the models, we created a performance metric that gives more importance to getting the top five and bottom three right and also rewarding correct positions elsewhere in the table giving us a `pm()` score. We also included a penalty for model complexity which by multiplying this by the score, we get our final performance metric, `pm_adjusted()`. Anna’s Poisson GLM received the highest adjusted score on the 2025/26 test season with a score of 0.565, so we used it to make our 2026/27 prediction. This score helped us compare our models, but it does not mean the prediction is guaranteed to be accurate.

We tried several types of models, including Poisson regression and Poisson GLMs, random forest regression, and a goal-ratio model. The different models used different information to estimate team performance, such as past goals, recent match results, and team attack and defence rankings.

For the 2026/27 prediction, we used actual results up to 19 October 2026 and predicted the results of the remaining matches. The model predicts that Manchester City will finish first, followed by Arsenal and Brighton. It places Chelsea and Liverpool in the rest of the top five. At the bottom of the table, it predicts Crystal Palace, Coventry and Sunderland in the relegation places, with Sunderland finishing last.

These results are only predictions and the final table could be different. Football is difficult to predict and the model cannot account for every change in team performance or unexpected event. Overall, our work let us compare different modelling approaches and use the one that performed best on our test season to make a prediction for 2026/27.
